name: Dysplasia Epiphysealis Hemimelica

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Dysplasia Epiphysealis Hemimelica

criteria.description: Presence of unilateral asymmetric epiphyseal overgrowth involving one or more epiphyses
Radiographic evidence of an irregular ossified mass arising from the epiphysis with continuity to underlying bone
Clinical presentation with painless or painful joint swelling and restricted range of motion
No histological evidence of malignancy or aggressive tumor features

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of unilateral epiphyseal overgrowth with characteristic radiographic ossified mass and compatible clinical presentation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathology is usually confirmatory but not always required if clinical and imaging features are typical.

searchTerms: unusual shape or structure of thigh bone
abnormal shape of thigh bone neck
loss of normal femoral head roundness

laboratory: Typically normal laboratory studies; no specific biomarkers identified
imaging: X-ray showing irregular ossified mass arising from epiphysis with continuity to underlying bone
MRI demonstrating cartilaginous cap and extent of epiphyseal involvement
CT scan for detailed bony architecture and surgical planning
genetic: No known consistent genetic mutations; sporadic cases predominating
other: Histopathology showing benign osteocartilaginous proliferation without malignant features

distinguishingFeatures: Osteochondroma arises from metaphysis rather than epiphysis
Typically presents as a solitary exostosis with cartilage cap
Usually asymptomatic unless impinging on structures
Multiple osteochondromas involving metaphyses of long bones
Positive family history and autosomal dominant inheritance
Benign bone tumor arising in epiphysis but with distinct radiographic and histologic features
Pain is more prominent and persistent
Radiographs show well-defined lytic lesion with sclerotic rim

redFlags: Rapid increase in size of epiphyseal mass
Neurological deficits or vascular compromise in affected limb
references: Schmale GA, Conrad EU 3rd, Raskind WH. Dysplasia epiphysealis hemimelica (Trevor disease): a report of 23 cases. J Bone Joint Surg Am. 1997
Azouz EM, Slomic AM, Marton D, Rigault P, Finidori G. The variable manifestations of dysplasia epiphysealis hemimelica. Pediatr Radiol. 1985
